newsitem.title: CZECH REPUBLIC: FOCUS-NOMURA PUTS TWIST IN BASS CZECH AIMS.
newsitem.headline: FOCUS-NOMURA PUTS TWIST IN BASS CZECH AIMS.

text.p: A unit of Nomura Intl. plc has thrown a twist into Bass plc's attempts to acquire a controlling share in the second largest Czech brewery Pivovar Radegast a.s. , by acquiring a 12.58 percent stake.

Transaction records published by the Czech Central Securities Registry (SCP) on Thursday showed Nomura Capital s.r.o., a Czech subsidiary of Nomura International plc , had acquired the Radegast shares.
Meanwhile shares in Radegast held by Czech bank IPB a.s. fell below the threshold for disclosure of 10 percent on July 3 from 19.53 percent on June 30.
Bass was seeking to raise its one-third stake in Radegast to a majority, and was in talks with IPB over a possible purchase, although IPB said publicly it was not for sale.

Records of transactions at the SCP reveal that 100,000 Radegast shares, a number equal to the stake Nomura acquired, traded over-the-counter in a block at 6,150 crowns per share on June 30. SCP records do not show counterparties in trades.

When asked about the transaction, IPB spokesman Jan Rezek would not directly confirm the deal took place, but he told Reuters: "It can be quite easily deduced from the circumstances." He referred any further comment to Nomura.
A spokesman in London for Nomura, which has been seeking to acquire a 36 percent stake in the bank IPB through a Czech government tender, also declined comment on the Radegast stake.

"What is going to happen, I am absolutely positive, is that Nomura is going to sell this to a strategic investor. That is why they entered the IPB tender in the first place, because IPB's stakes in companies were attractive to them," said Eric Volkman, equity analyst at Raiffesisen Capital in Prague.
"It wouldn't surprise me if Bass eventually got it. Nomura has no interest in breweries as far as I understand."
Graham Staley, Bass's country manager said on the Radegast sale: "Bass has no comment as this is not a matter for Bass. This is an internal matter for IPB."
Radegast shares rose 21 crowns to 3,561 at the Prague Stock Exchange on Thursday.
Rezek also confirmed a story on Thursday in the Czech daily Mlada Fronta Dnes which said that IPB has divested some of its stakes in several large companies recently.
This included shares in another brewer, Plzensky Prazdroj a.s. to Netherlands-registered Quartermaine Investment Fund.
Nomura's spokesman, Stephen Jolly, refused to comment on whether Nomura had any connection to Quartermaine.
Nomura recently has been working closely in financial deals with IPB, and another subsidiary Nutshell s.r.o. holds a five percet stake in the Czech bank.
